facts.label: Because, so e but
facts.sub: Because dá a razão. So dá o resultado. But dá o contraste. Use o passado para contar sentimentos.

facts.label: Porque
facts.sub: Use because para dar o motivo: I was upset because my brother forgot my birthday. Depois de because vem uma frase completa, com sujeito e verbo no passado.

facts.label: Então
facts.sub: Use so para dar o resultado de algo: I was angry, so I didn’t answer. Coloque uma vírgula antes de so. A primeira parte é a causa; a segunda, o resultado.

compare.br: No Brasil, dizemos “porque”, “então” e “mas” em frases curtas.

compare.us: Em inglês, because dá a razão, so dá o resultado e but dá o contraste.

solo: Peça uma experiência pessoal do aluno com essa diferença.

pages.title: A rainy day and a hard feeling · 1/3
paragraphs: It is a gray Saturday morning in Seattle. Bruno sits by the window with a cup of tea. His friend Theo comes in with wet shoes. Bruno is in a bad mood today. He is disappointed, and he does not hide his feeling. Theo asks him to tell the whole story.

“I was upset yesterday because my brother forgot my birthday.” says Bruno. “That is sad. Did he call you later, or was he too busy?” says Theo. “He called at night, but I was angry, so I didn’t answer.” says Bruno.
